name: Erebus Siphon

detectability.signature: A deep-frequency gravity hum that sharpens into a rising whine as the well inhales

proximity: Course corrections fail silently as trajectories curve toward the focus
Sensor returns double-track every contact in the volume
contact: Hull plating groans under mounting tidal stress
Engines deliver full thrust while the ship still loses ground
prolonged_exposure: Structural collapse from sustained differential pull
Terminal descent into the crush zone at the focus

phenomena: Objects accelerating toward the focus without any visible thrust
Background starlight smearing into arcs during peak pull
Dust streams drawing long bright filaments into the well
hazards: Structural collapse from tidal forces at peak pull
Navigation system failure during intensification phases
opportunities: Energy harvesting potential from the gravitationally compressed debris stream
Strategic chokepoint control over the surrounding corridor
known_incidents: The hauler Merciful Ox spent eleven hours climbing out of the well at full burn and arrived with her keel permanently bowed
Rival salvage crews have fought pitched battles over debris trapped at the pull boundary
description: Erebus Siphon announces itself as a slow spiral of dust and frozen propellant wound tight around a focus no telescope can resolve. The region spans nearly an astronomical unit, an invisible funnel printed in debris across space. Sensors translate its presence into a deep, patient hum that crews feel in their teeth before any instrument agrees.

The well breathes. On a roughly thirty-one-hour cycle its pull intensifies, drawing loose matter inward in long luminous filaments before relaxing again. Trajectories bend toward the focus even under full engine burn, and veteran pilots time their transits to the exhale. The pattern is reliable enough to chart and treacherous enough to kill anyone who trusts it twice.

Discovered when a convoy's lead ship simply stopped making headway against empty space, the Siphon has claimed hulls slowly rather than dramatically; most victims ran out of fuel, not structure. Salvage syndicates camp along its boundary, picking clean the debris the well coughs back up. Its steady rhythm has made it a natural tollgate for the corridor it dominates.

Energy concerns now anchor collection arrays along the infall stream, siphoning the siphon. Cartographers re-measure its cycle annually, watching for drift no model predicts. Whoever controls the exhale windows controls everything that moves through this stretch of dark.
